critique: The timing now reads as a localized seed release: t1 is a compact cluster and t4 becomes a distinctly rightward, widening plume. This is much closer to blowing seeds than the prior broad birth field. However, the plume remains undersized and faint within the frame, with the dandelion sprites reading as tiny upright seed-head silhouettes rather than a clearly legible, airy cloud. The t4 distribution also has somewhat more downward/backward scatter than a clean wind-carried sweep.

suggestions.why: Increase seed silhouette size so the botanical particles read clearly at thumbnail scale rather than as a dim, tiny cluster.
Fill the plume moderately while retaining the localized origin and avoiding the sparse gaps visible at t4.
Tighten directional spread to reduce backward and excessive vertical scatter, making the expanding cloud read more consistently as wind-blown rightward dispersal.
